newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaragua's Aleman to inherit lower foreign debt.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua's Aleman to inherit lower foreign debt.

text.p: Nicaragua's incoming government, which takes power January 10, will inherit a greatly reduced foreign debt of $3.8 billion, a top minister said on Wednesday.

When President Violeta Chamorro took power in 1990, upsetting former Sandinista President Daniel Ortega at the ballot box, she inherited a $12 billion debt, more than six times the country's gross domestic product, Foreign Cooperation Minister Erwin Krueger told a news conference.
Since then, through the renegotiation of its debt with donor countries and the buy-back of commercial debt, the Chamorro administration has cut a huge chunk of that total.
Earlier this year Russia pardoned $3.3 billion in Nicaraguan debt, and Nicaragua is trying to renegotiate its $860 million debt to other Central American countries.
Chamorro will pass the presidential sash on to right-winger Arnoldo Aleman of the Liberal Alliance. He is expected to continue the broad outlines of Chamorro's economic policy.
Despite the reduction of the debt, Krueger said Nicaragua under Aleman will still be dependent on foreign aid to balance its budget.

"While Nicaragua doesn't manage to close the gap in its balance of payments it will be dependent on foreign aid," he said. "The economy, in spite of the recent advances, is fragile. It will need aid in the area of $500 million a year for the next five years."
Among the advances of the Chamorro governemt listed by Krueger were the reduction of inflation, which reached 33,000 percent a year in 1990, to about 9.6 percent in 1996. It was 11.2 percent in 1995.
The Nicaraguan economy shrank by 2.5 percent in 1990 following five years of steady decline, but will grow by 5.5 percent in 1996, he said.
